values.title: Day of AI Australia: Teacher Insights from a Nation-Wide AI Literacy Program for K-12 Students (Banks and Renzella; pp. 1375-1376; published 2025-02-18 per Crossref)
values.teachers_in_program: 370 teachers from 260 schools (2024 DoAIA); the poster does not give a number of 'classes'
values.rating_scale: Likert 1 = Strongly Disagree, 5 = Strongly Agree; per-lesson means 4.08-4.75
values.other_stats: 78% reported increased teaching confidence; 85% reported high engagement; 92% willing to teach again
values.stated_limitations: No dedicated limitations section. Poster itself states: 'preliminary data'; participation skewed ('89.7% of students came from Major cities'; independent and Catholic schools 'over-represented'; lower engagement from regional and public schools). Feedback is teacher self-report, anonymous, aggregated. No explicit statement about the response rate or non-response bias of the 61 teachers.
quotes: Over 64,000 students and 370 teachers from 260 schools across Australia participated in the 2024 DoAIA.
61 teachers responded to the forms, representing around 2,946 students.
Likert rating scale where 1 = Strongly Disagree, and 5 = Strongly Agree
89.7% of students came from Major cities.

I read no repository files and ran no git commands. The Crossref records carry no received/accepted dates (assertion list has none), so those come from the ScienceDirect article-history data only. Crossref 'published-online' is null for both Elsevier articles; the Available online date is corroborated by ScienceDirect citation_online_date and the Crossref created date. ScienceDirect lists Version of Record two to one days after Available online for both articles.
